extension.summary: Create custom TV channels from your Kodi library
extension.description: Turn your own Kodi library into channels that play like broadcast TV. Build TV show channels (round robin or serial), movie, folder, audio and party channels, each with a rolling queue that is topped up as items play. Mix channels together by interleaving items from other channels, combine different content in Combo Blocks, schedule blocks of programming, and let a channel resume where you left off. Works with the local files in your library and with shared network storage.
extension.news: 3.1.168: in the side panel, pressing Enter right after it opens now plays the highlighted channel; before, the first Enter did nothing until you moved up or down. 3.1.167: the Kodi log no longer fills with "error reading the default value" lines for the side-panel start-channel setting (it was about nine lines in ten in some logs). Nothing about playback changed. 3.1.166: switching from the plain channel list back to the side panel (Use side panel setting) now works without restarting Kodi. 3.1.165: the draw journal now keeps 5 days (was 14); its bulky state-save lines are written only when Log level is Debug; the log now explains a failed backup or journal copy (what the share looked like, how long after a video stopped, where an error happened). 3.1.164: new setting Advanced > "Channel list opens on" (first channel, the last channel played on this device, or a channel you choose) for the side panel; the add-on now uses Kodi's newer video-info calls for channel and queue listings; the Log level setting is now a Warning / Info / Debug choice and really controls what is written to the Kodi log (leave it on Info while testing). 3.1.163: the side panel's channel list has a "Channels:" heading at the top, and each channel now shows a second line with its next item (for example "Next: Bones · S3E4 · 42 in queue"; movies show "Title (Year)"). Look only; nothing about playback changed. 3.1.162: the side panel's selection bar is shorter and has rounded corners, with a small rounded tab at its left edge. Look only; nothing about playback changed. 3.1.161: the side panel's bars and backgrounds were never drawn (the texture they named did not exist), so the new blue selection bar did not show; the add-on now ships its own white texture and uses it. Look only; nothing about playback changed. 3.1.160: the side panel looks bigger and clearer: larger channel names and subtitles, a solid bright-blue selection bar with white text (no more yellow), a little space between rows, larger channel icons. Look only; nothing about playback changed. 3.1.159: Missing Durations now also lists episodes and movies played with the default length because nothing gave their real length (marked "default length used"), and shows the show's name for episodes; the daily library update no longer rebuilds the library file when it was rebuilt within the last hour. 3.1.158: Reset Show in the side panel now asks for confirmation and refuses when another device is playing the channel (like the Kodi list); the Auto-Create "library not ready" message names the right place (Settings > Cache); the cursor-shrink warning no longer fires for a long show that simply wrapped to its first episode. 3.1.157: the library lists now reload on every device when the shared library file changes (the check from 3.1.156 never fired); the log says when a show wraps back to its first episode instead of warning of a lost position; the journal's end-of-playback records name the right item. 3.1.156: new setting (Settings > Cache, off by default): once a day, at a time you choose, one device rebuilds the shared library file, fixes queued file paths and puts back missing shows; channels being played are skipped and retried every hour. 3.1.155: new setting (Settings > Channels, off by default): scheduled block items that nobody watched are removed when their time slot ends, so a missed block no longer waits at the front; a carousel channel leaves its clock alone while a block is at the front. 3.1.154: Rebuild Queue, Keep Places no longer carries a random pick over as the place of a Combo show that was switched to sequential, and starts a new sequential Combo show at its starting point; editing a Combo slot now keeps the order of its shows. 3.1.153: new channel menu item "Rebuild Queue, Keep Places" (on channels with something woven into them): rebuilds the queue so an edited Combo Block shows up at once while every show keeps its place; nothing is reset. 3.1.152: editing a Combo Block TV slot now keeps its episodes-per-turn numbers (with the same keep / change / set-only-new question as TV channels) and no longer drops shows the filter does not match; TV and Movie slots with a filter can also add titles outside the filter. 3.1.151: when you edit a TV channel that already plays more than one episode per turn for some show, you are now asked whether to keep those numbers, change them for every show, or (if you added shows) set only the new ones, instead of going through every show. 3.1.150: when you create or edit a TV or movie channel with a filter you can now also add shows or movies that the filter does not match (a question after the filter, default No); editing a filter-built TV channel no longer drops the shows the filter does not match; Select Specific Movies on a filter-built movie channel ticks only what the channel plays. 3.1.149: logging only: a device no longer logs "folder not reachable" once a minute for a file that is simply not there yet (seen on the PVR PC and a Shield). 3.1.148: devices that share a folder now take a lock (a small file, mutex.dat) while they save, so two devices can no longer overwrite each other's carousel pops or positions; if the lock is busy for two seconds the device saves anyway. Setting: Network > Lock the shared folder while saving. 3.1.147: logging only: every carousel clock write now records the clock it replaced and the queue file's time and size, and a clock that moves forward without a pop claim on that device is journalled as clock_jump with the code path that wrote it. 3.1.146: optional timing master: one device (Settings > Network) pops the carousel while it is running and the others only keep the clock of the channel they play; each carousel channel's clock and pop claim now live in a small file of its own, so another device's save of state.json can no longer erase it. 3.1.145: a save can no longer lower a carousel clock below one this device saw on the share in the last two minutes, so a device that reads an old or empty state.json cannot erase clocks. 3.1.142: a carousel channel is no longer popped twice for one interval when two devices check it a few seconds apart; the claim now stops a device whose clock is older than the shared one, and a save can no longer lower a carousel clock. More journal lines (claim decisions, kept clocks, who wrote state.json, stale reads, device sleep, journal copy failures). 3.1.141: if another device's save erases a carousel pop's clock, the pop writes it again, so the channel no longer runs one episode ahead of its clock. 3.1.140: a draw journal records every episode pop, draw and position change on each device (and keeps the last Kodi log of each restart) so problems can be traced from the files; Backup includes it. 3.1.139: the show order question (keep, shuffle, manual) is now also asked for TV channels that play random episodes, and the shuffled order is shown in a scrolling list of every show. 3.1.138: an episode whose .nfo cannot be read is queued with its Kodi running time (or a default length from Settings) instead of being skipped, so a brief network failure no longer makes a show lose episodes; Studio filters can be typed ("contains Universal") for TV Shows and Movies. 3.1.137: a channel restarted after an unplayable file now comes to full screen even when Kodi's "failed to play" message is showing (cold start from the side panel). 3.1.136: a channel restarted after an unplayable file is checked for several seconds and brought to full screen if it plays behind the home screen; extra log lines record what Kodi is showing. 3.1.135: a channel restarted after an unplayable file comes back to full screen; Kodi no longer waits 5 seconds for the add-on service when you close it while a channel is playing. 3.1.134: pressing Stop at the exact moment an episode ends can no longer freeze the add-on service. 3.1.133: fixes the freeze when a missing file is reached at the moment an episode ends; the missing item is now skipped and the channel keeps playing. 3.1.132: "Play from this item" now skips the items in front of it like the Next button (each is replaced by the next episode of its show) instead of moving them to the end, so episodes no longer run out of order; an episode whose file is missing is skipped and logged, and the channel keeps playing. 3.1.131: a scheduled block that fires while you are watching the channel is no longer lost, even when the next episode starts very early. Earlier changes are listed in CHANGELOG.md.
